summary: The source permits at most 100 elements, which is too narrow for honest runtime scaling, while wrapping a descending permutation to ascending order has a matching linear mutation lower bound.

optimality.argument: For a descending array of distinct values, the next permutation is its ascending reversal and all but at most one of the n positions must change, giving an Omega(n) worst-case lower bound. The implementation performs one pivot scan, at most one successor scan, and one suffix reversal, so its upper bound is O(n).

replacement_checks.evidence: A legal in-place wraparound from a strictly descending array to its ascending arrangement must inspect and rewrite a linear number of positions.
Each scan is monotone and each suffix position participates in at most one swap, with only fixed scalar state.

Regression traverses complete lexicographic cycles for every array through length eight over four values, then checks ascending and descending arrays at every legal length in both app-local and immutable native sources.
